output.title: When date ambiguity stops working
output.body:
If you run a small business, date ambiguity stops being a minor annoyance when it keeps interrupting one recurring workflow. The question is not whether AI can read a date. The question is whether you keep losing time to missing time zones, mixed formats, or two systems that disagree on the same deadline.

The useful decision is bounded: keep checking dates manually, hire someone to watch the queue, or automate one narrow step that standardises dates at the point of entry and flags anything unclear before it spreads. That is a fit check, not a promise. If dates come from one source in one format, the problem may be smaller than it looks. If they come from email, forms, spreadsheets, and memory, the mess will keep inventing itself. Very considerate, in a hostile way.

A practical next step is simple: watch one recurring workflow for a week and count every pause caused by date ambiguity. Note whether the issue is a missing timezone, an unclear format, or conflicting sources. If the same confusion keeps showing up, you have a repeatable control problem. Then you can decide whether a bounded automation is worth considering, while keeping human approval in charge for anything high-risk.
